pages.text: "I'll clear it first!" Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, set a sled on the snow and ran. A thick log blocked the middle of the sledding path. "I'll move it alone! The first ride is mine!"

Ppino pushed a shoulder against the log. Heave! It didn't budge. Rudi the hungry squirrel came up with a sled. "Shall we push together?" Ppino didn't answer, just pressed their lips tight and pushed harder.
Ppino braced their feet and pushed again. Heave, heave! Only the orange shoes slid over the snow. Three pushes, and the log stayed there. Ppino dropped into the snow.
Below, the morning bell rang. Dong! Grandma Bear, who ran the lodge, came uphill. "Is the log heavy, Ppino?" "I should be able to push it... but it won't move." Ppino's long ears flopped sideways.
Grandma put a hand at one end. "Two hands, twice the strength. Six hands, six times." Rudi hurried to hold the middle. Ppino put their hands on the other end.
Grandma took a deep breath and counted. "One, two, three—push!" All three drove their shoulders forward together. The log rolled and sank into the snow. The sledding path opened wide.
"It's open!" Ppino's ears leaned forward first. "One, two, three—push!" Rudi and Grandma pushed from behind. The sled zoomed down the slope.
Far below, Ppino waved and shouted. "I've never gone this far!" A single sled track stretched behind, right from the top. Up there, Rudi and Grandma waved back.
Ppino put both hands behind Rudi's sled. "One, call if I can't do it alone! Two, each take a place! Three, count together, push together!" Rudi looked back over a shoulder and smiled.
Rudi wrapped an arm around Ppino's shoulders as they pulled their sleds side by side. What one can't push rolls away with many hands. "Together tomorrow too! One, two, three—push!" Ppino called.
